gloss: tatsuta-age; chicken or fish marinated in soy and fried with starch coating

definitions.explanation: Bite-sized pieces of chicken or fish marinated in soy sauce, mirin, and ginger, then dusted in potato starch and deep-fried. The reddish-brown color of the surface is said to resemble autumn leaves on the Tatsuta River.

examples.japanese: {昼食|ちゅうしょく}に{竜田|たつた}{揚|あ}げを{作|つく}った。
{鶏|とり}{肉|にく}の{竜田|たつた}{揚|あ}げはお{弁当|べんとう}の{定番|ていばん}だ。
examples.english: Chicken tatsuta-age is a standard item in bento boxes.

examples.japanese: {竜田|たつた}{揚|あ}げは{下味|したあじ}をしっかりつけてから{揚|あ}げると、{冷|さ}めてもおいしい。
examples.english: Tatsuta-age stays tasty even after it cools if you marinate it well before frying.

notes:
Name comes from the {竜田川|たつたがわ} (Tatsuta River) in Nara, famous in classical poetry for its red autumn maple leaves — the soy-marinated surface turns a similar reddish brown after frying.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鶏|とり}の{竜田|たつた}{揚|あ}げ: chicken tatsuta-age
- {鯖|さば}の{竜田|たつた}{揚|あ}げ: mackerel tatsuta-age
- {竜田|たつた}{揚|あ}げ{弁当|べんとう}: tatsuta-age bento

SIMILAR WORDS:
- から{揚|あ}げ: karaage — also marinated, fried chicken, but the coating is usually flour or a mix; soy marination is lighter. The line between karaage and tatsuta-age is blurry, and many recipes overlap.
- {天|てん}ぷら: tempura — uses a batter rather than a dry starch coating; not marinated
